providers.title: Pretree
providers.scope: A set with a ternary betweenness relation satisfying four axioms that hold for the vertices of a tree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Four points in a row
providers.scope: Three implications that place four points of a pretree in a row.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals along a chain
providers.scope: The interval between the ends of a finite sequence of points lies in the union of the intervals between consecutive points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Finite pretrees and finite trees
providers.scope: Every finite pretree is a set of vertices of a finite tree with the betweenness of the tree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cycles of adjacent points
providers.scope: Distinct points of a pretree that are cyclically adjacent are pairwise adjacent.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Directions
providers.scope: A linear subset of a pretree with two chosen points has exactly one direction in which the first precedes the second.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals are ordered
providers.scope: A closed interval of a pretree is an arc, ordered from one end to the other, and its ends are determined by it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniqueness of medians
providers.scope: Three points of a pretree have at most one median.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Half-open intervals
providers.scope: In a dense pretree, two half-open intervals with the same closed end that are equal have the same open end.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Complete and dense does not imply median
providers.scope: A tripod with a half-open segment next to the centre removed on one leg is a complete dense pretree in which three points have no median and an interval has a cut that is not made at a point.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ends of half-open intervals
providers.scope: In a dense median pretree, if the half-open interval from x to y lies in the closed interval from x to z, then y lies in it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cuts are made at points
providers.scope: In a complete dense median pretree, every partition of a closed interval into two arcs is made at a point of the interval.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals have no gaps
providers.scope: In a complete dense median pretree every nonempty subset of a closed interval has a least upper bound in the interval.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Gates
providers.scope: In a tree, the path from a vertex to a point of a given path passes through the gate of the vertex, and the path between two vertices with different gates runs through both gates.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: From weakly to strongly dense
providers.scope: In a median pretree the medians of triples from a weakly dense set form a strongly dense set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cantor's theorem
providers.scope: Any two nonempty countable dense totally ordered sets without ends are order isomorphic.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Order type of intervals
providers.scope: In a complete separable median pretree every interval with distinct ends is order isomorphic to the real interval [0,1].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Intervals are arcs
providers.scope: Under the assumptions of the theorem, every interval of the pretree with distinct ends is homeomorphic to the real interval [0,1], by an order isomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Small intervals
providers.scope: Every neighbourhood of a point contains the intervals from that point to all points of a smaller neighbourhood.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Countable base
providers.scope: The sets H(p,q) with p, q in a countable strongly dense set form a subbase of the topology, so the space is metrizable.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dendrites from pretrees
providers.scope: A compact space with a countable dense subset carrying a complete dense median pretree structure with open sets H(x,y) is a dendrite, and the pretree intervals are its only arcs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
